injection_contract.principle: A Visual Referee is a third pixel witness on a LOCAL question the deterministic layer has already reduced to an enumerated set of candidates. It never creates geometry, never moves a coordinate, never sees a published figure, never ranks readings, and its answer re-enters the pipeline only by changing the deterministic input of one seam (e.g. a WEAK gap becoming STRONG or NONE), after which every existing gate, policy comparison and resolver rule runs unchanged.
injection_contract.recommended_seam: Model it on the 005H LabelRecogniser seam, not on VisionReasoner: a pixel-only crop type with a fixed field list (packages/source-metrics/src/recogniser.ts L24-77), a pure decision rule between the deterministic reading and the external one (packages/source-metrics/src/ensemble.ts L91-156), pinned model/runtime hashes, a stability bracket of crop variants, and architecture tests that pin the input fields and the call order (tests/architecture/recogniser.test.ts L40-119).
interface_sketch: type RefereeQuestionKind = OPENING_VS_PATTERN | GAP_INFILL | INFILL_VS_PAVING_EDGE | POST_VS_PIER | GAP_SPLIT | ... (one closed answer enum per kind, each including UNRESOLVED)

type RefereeCrop = { key: string /* opaque q0,q1,... */; kind: RefereeQuestionKind; rgb: { width, height, data } /* the frame's own pixels, axis-aligned, no resampling, off-frame = paper */; marks: Array<{ role: JAMB_A|JAMB_B|SPAN|SUBJECT|CANDIDATE_A|CANDIDATE_B; rect: PixelRect /* crop px */ }>; wallPx: number /* a drawing-relative size cue, never metres */ } - and no other field

type RefereeReading = { key; engine; modelSha256; runtime; answers: Array<{ answer: string; p: number }>; variants: Array<{ variant: BASE|PAD|TRIM|SCALE90; top: string; p: number }>; stable: boolean }

interface VisualReferee { id; model: { name; sha256 }; runtime; runtimeSha256?; judge(crops: readonly RefereeCrop[], options?: { signal?; onProgress? }): Promise<RefereeReading[]>; release?(): Promise<void> }

refereeRuleOf(deterministic: { questionId; candidates: string[]; current: string; strength: STRONG|WEAK|NONE }, reading): { decision: AGREES|SETTLES|CONTESTS|NOT_CONFIDENT|UNRESOLVED; chosen?: string; why } - pure, imports only the seam types
injection_contract.where_it_runs: Two-pass, because reconstructV2 is synchronous (packages/reconstruction/src/v2/reconstruct-v2.ts L161; called without await at packages/analysis-service/src/run.ts L397) and the questions exist only after decomposePlan: pass 1 = today's deterministic run, which also emits RefereeQuestion records (stable ids from frame variantByteHash + seam geometry, e.g. the existing gap id boundary-evidence.ts L450); the service asks the referee once per frame batch (like extractMetricEvidenceAsync's generator, packages/source-metrics/src/extract.ts L314-332, L447); pass 2 reruns reconstructV2 with refereeAnswers: ReadonlyMap<questionId, RefereeDecision>. With no referee the run is pass 1 only and byte-identical to today.
question_generation_rules: Questions are generated for EVERY instance of a seam kind on every plan copy the solver decomposes (selected copy and resolver copies alike), never for a subset chosen by a score, a footprint bucket, a resolver rank or the published figure.

Only seams whose deterministic state is a local deferral or near tie are asked: UNKNOWN_GAP/WEAK (boundary-evidence.ts L460, L469, L479-481), the GLAZING->DASHED override (L444-446), runsPast loose disagreement (L455-460), POST/WALL parts adjacent to a gap (L116), wide openings decided OPEN_SIDE (plan-decomposition.ts L1445), AMBIGUOUS labels (axis-topology.ts L452-453).
Budget by count, sorted by stable question id (counts, never a clock - plan-resolution.ts L90-91 convention); over-budget questions are recorded as unasked.

The crop is cut from the same raster the seam read (layout.ts L353-355), around the seam's own pixel geometry, with fixed margins in wall thicknesses; the marks are the deterministic candidates' geometry.
validation: Reject the whole reading unless: key echoes a question asked; answers are within the kind's closed enum; p in [0,1]; all four crop variants present (stability bracket, cf. EXTERNAL_VARIANTS recogniser.ts L37-39).
Confident only when top p >= a bound fixed BEFORE any benchmark (cf. OCR_ENSEMBLE_BOUNDS 0.9, ensemble.ts L58-59) AND stable across variants; otherwise NOT_CONFIDENT -> no effect.
UNRESOLVED is a first-class answer and has no effect.
Model and runtime pinned by SHA-256 in a manifest checked at load (as numeric-recogniser-ort); a changed file is refused (cf. ASSETS_REFUSED, errors.ts L118).
application_rule: SETTLES only where the deterministic state is WEAK/AMBIGUOUS/deferred and the answer names one of the already enumerated candidates (e.g. UNKNOWN_GAP -> OPENING_SUPPORTED/STRONG or TRUE_EXTERIOR_GAP/NONE; DASHED override -> keep GLAZING or keep DASHED).

Against a STRONG deterministic decision the answer can only CONTEST (recorded as doubt, optionally demoting STRONG->WEAK) - never flip it (ensemble.ts L25-35 precedent: "neither wins because it is external").
It never adds a gap, a band, a body, a coordinate or a callout, and never changes a threshold.

Its effect is applied before boundary policies are compared, so BOUNDARY_RESOLUTION_INCONCLUSIVE, completion guards (NO_CONTINUATION etc.), layout gate and plan resolver all re-run on the changed inputs exactly as today.
non_circularity: Never sees: published facts/areas/rooms (do NOT reuse VisionContextFact - packages/source-analyzer/src/analyze.ts L97, L195 pass pkg.publishedFacts to every vision request), metres, scale, other readings, policy areas, resolver scores, footprint buckets, frame/asset ids, URLs, captions, project names.

Is NOT a resolver Corroboration: plan-resolution.ts L97-98 defines a corroboration as "neither the published figure nor the pixels the reading was made from" - the referee reads the same pixels, so it must not be added to corroborations (L417-423) and must not change PublishedFigureUse (L105, L536). The figure keeps its "refuse the first reading or choose among the others, never both" rule (L56-72).
Decoy-footprint control (plan-resolution.ts L56-60: figure x1.25 / x0.8) must produce identical questions, crops and answers.
Order invariance: shuffled frames/questions give identical answers (005I §G: 135 frames x 24 shuffles precedent).
